title: Scoped Security Onboarding: Acceptance Criteria and Rollback Playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description: This ticket defines a scoped Product Requirements Document (PRD) and acceptance checklist for onboarding enterprise customers requiring SSO (SAML + OIDC), RBAC, exhaustive audit logging, and customer-managed key capabilities (KMS/HSM). It also defines a staged rollout and a concrete rollback playbook intended for Dedicated and Private deployments. The goal is to create an interoperable, testable, auditable onboarding path that meets SOC2/ISO controls and minimizes production blast radius.
background_and_goals: Several inbound customer requests and pre-sales evaluations identified gaps in the current Private onboarding flow: (1) inconsistent SAML metadata validation across operator workflows, (2) under-specified RBAC role mappings for tenant isolation, (3) missing end-to-end audit assertions for cross-component key usage, and (4) unclear operator rollback steps when KMS/HSM binding fails. Goals: reduce time-to-onboard by 30%, ensure all onboarding steps produce immutable audit evidence, and enable safe automatic rollback of changes that would break crypto bindings or auth flows.
scope_included:
- SSO: SAML integration with metadata validation, SP-initiated and IdP-initiated login tests, OIDC optional; SCIM for user provisioning as stretch goal.
- RBAC: tenant role matrix (Owner, Admin, Dev, Observer), mapping guidance for IDP groups, API tokens tied to roles.
- Audit logs: immutable audit trail for auth events, key events (create/rotate/destroy), admin role changes; retention settings per customer.
- KMS/HSM: support for customer-managed KMS (AWS/GCP/Azure) and HSM operator mode; key binding verification and rotation hooks.
- Rollout: staged canary across 3 private accounts with automatic failover and manual rollback playbook.
scope_out_of_scope:
- Building a brand new identity provider; we will integrate with customer IdPs via standard protocols only.
- Deep SCIM feature parity (only basic provisioning supported initially).
- Air-gapped physical HSM delivery (operations will be documented but hardware procurement is customer-managed).
requirements_clarifications:
- Clarify canonical set of SAML attributes customers must provide (uid, email, groups) and fallback rules.
- Define maximum acceptable auth latency impact (SLO: 300ms additional at median).
- KMS key policies need to allow Redwood operator verification calls; we require ephemeral verification role or signed assertion.
- RBAC model must permit both group-to-role and claim-to-role mappings; define precedence rules when both exist.
open_questions: Do we require mandatory SCIM provisioning for P0 customers or allow manual invite flows?
Which HSM vendors are in scope for operator test harness (YubiHSM, Luna, Azure Dedicated HSM)?
Should audit logs be shipped to customer-managed S3/Blob by default or stored in Redwood with export hooks?
What are minimum encryption-at-rest cipher suites mandated for private deployments?
acceptance_criteria: SSO: Successful end-to-end SAML login (SP-initiated and IdP-initiated) in customer test tenant documented with SAML traces and response verification logs.
RBAC: Role mapping test cases executed demonstrating least-privilege enforcement for Owner/Admin/Dev/Observer across API and Console actions.
Audit logs: Proof of immutable audit entries for auth and key lifecycle events with sampling demonstrated in the observability console and via exported bundle.
KMS/HSM: Key binding verification completed for at least one customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS) and one HSM flow; rotation initiated and verified end-to-end without service outage.
Operator playbook: Runbook executed in a dry-run on staging where a simulated bad IdP metadata payload triggers rollback and operator alerts, with postmortem logged.
SLOs: Auth end-to-end latency degradation under test remains within defined SLO (median + 300ms).
Security review: Product and Security signoff obtained; any findings tracked and resolved or accepted in risk register.
signoff_checklist: PM signoff (Aisha Patel): acceptance criteria validated against customer test case matrix.
Security signoff (Lead Security Engineer): threat model and risk acceptance signed; remaining issues listed with mitigation plan.
Infra/Ops signoff: Operator runbook validated on 3 staging clusters and rollback steps tested.
Eng signoff: Automated test coverage >= 80% for onboarding flows and smoke tests for RBAC enforcement.
Legal/Compliance: Data residency and audit retention schedule approved for target customers.
Customer success: Knowledge transfer document and onboarding checklist published to internal playbooks.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Internal validation on staging cluster (Week 1) -> Phase 2: Canary with 3 pilot customers in Private (Week 2-3) -> Phase 3: Broader private rollout with opt-in flag and telemetry (Week 4). Each phase includes a mandatory rollback dry-run. Rollback triggers: failed key-binding verification, missing immutable audit evidence, or repeated auth failures (>5% error rate over 10 minutes).
rollback_playbook:
1) Detect: alert triggers from KMS binding or auth error thresholds.
2) Quarantine: automatically pause new onboarding flows to the affected region/tenant and ramp down traffic to canary nodes.
3) Revert: apply last known-good config snapshot for IdP metadata/RBAC mapping.
4) Key handling: if KMS binding failed during rotation, restore prior key alias and revoke ephemeral credentials.
5) Postmortem: collect SAML traces, audit bundles, and operator logs; run incident review within 72 hours.
6) Customer comms: templated notice for affected customers with rollback summary and mitigation steps.
test_scenarios: SAML attribute omission: IdP omits groups attribute -> system maps default observer role and logs consent warning.
KMS rotation failure: simulate rotation error during rotation hook and verify automatic rebind to previous key and no loss of decryption capability.
RBAC precedence: user with conflicting group and claim roles receives most-restrictive effective permissions per precedence rule; verified via API and console attempts.
Audit integrity: attempt to tamper with local audit file; system detects signature mismatch and surfaces integrity alert in console.
dependencies: ENG-92214: identity-metadata-validation-lib (must be merged before canary)
risks_and_mitigations:
- Risk: Misconfigured IdP metadata could lock out tenant admins. Mitigation: provide a safety rollback that preserves a single emergency admin account bound by email verification.
- Risk: Key rotation could cause decryption gaps. Mitigation: require pre-rotation verification and staged rotation with fallback alias.
- Risk: Audit log leakage to shared storage. Mitigation: default to customer-managed storage or encrypted per-tenant buckets with strict IAM policies.
